name: Yellow-bellied Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern canada and usa; winters mexico to panama
description: Small flycatcher, extremely similar to several other species. Generally shy and inconspicuous; breeds in spruce forests often near boggy areas.

name: Baudo Oropendola
rangeDescription: Northeastern colombia (northern chocó)
description: This impressively large and colorful oropendola is found only in lowland and foothill rainforest in northwestern Colombia. Its salmon-colored cheek patches along with chestnut back and belly distinguish it from Black Oropendola; also note the yellow tail and orange bill tip.

name: Rufous-eared Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Andes of northwestern peru (cajamarca, la libertad, ancash, and huánuco)
description: Uncommon brushfinch restricted to the high Andes of northern and central Peru. Adult is mostly gray with a chestnut cap, black-and-white mustache stripes, and a white spot in front of the eye.

name: Imperial Snipe
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of colombia to eastern peru
description: Hulking snipe of high-elevation elfin forest in the Andes. Large with a thick, drooping bill.

name: Gray-crowned Munia
rangeDescription: New guinea (kurik and mapa areas to lower fly river)
description: A small bird of lowland grasslands in the Trans-Fly of New Guinea. Gray-brown back, white head, black throat.

name: Beautiful Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of southern mexico (guerrero and southern puebla to eastern oaxaca)
description: Small hummingbird of desert scrub and brushy woodland in dry interior areas of southwest Mexico. Feeds quietly at all levels, often on cactus flowers.

name: Stub-tailed Spadebill
rangeDescription: Tropical southern mexico to western costa rica and northwestern panama
description: Tiny ‘cute’ flycatcher found in fairly open but shady understory of tropical lowland forest, mainly in humid areas. Appearance is distinctive, with brownish upperparts, striking face pattern, and stubby tail.

name: Eared Quetzal
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western mexico; occasional southeastern arizona
description: Scarce, large trogon of pine and pine-oak forests in mountains and canyons of northwest Mexico. Usually rather wary, flying long distances when disturbed, but can be found feeding quietly at fruiting trees.

name: Puerto Rican Tanager
rangeDescription: Highlands of puerto rico
description: A noisy, gregarious species of middle to high elevation forests where it often forms mixed-species flocks. Typically roosts communally in palm or bamboo thickets.

name: Violet-throated Metaltail
rangeDescription: Páramo of andes of south-central ecuador (azuay)
description: High-elevation hummingbird endemic to the Andes of southern Ecuador. Plumage is mostly green with a purple throat, and tail is blue on top and greenish underneath.

name: White-throated Mountain-Babbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern nigeria and southwestern cameroon
description: A strange, chunky rusty-brown forest babbler with a white face and throat, pale blue-gray eyes, and a pale bill, rendering it unmistakable. Juvenile has a browner throat.

name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Eastern north america (southern canada to texas and florida keys)
description: Medium-sized woodpecker that is not well named; rarely is the slight red wash on the belly visible! Instead, note the black-and-white barring on the back and wings, plain buffy breast and face, and red nape.

name: Red-and-black Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and eastern amazonian brazil
description: Medium-sized shy bird of tall forest. Both sexes easily recognizable by thick conical bill and contrasting black head; male’s red plumage renders it essentially unmistakable.

name: Jamaican Tody
rangeDescription: Hills and mountains of jamaica
description: A small, gemlike, woodland species usually found in pairs. Its rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a unique profile.

name: Yellow-eared Bulbul
rangeDescription: Highlands of sri lanka
description: Medium-sized, plump green bulbul with a yellow belly and distinctive head pattern with yellow tufts behind each eye, white tufts above each eye, and white horns sticking up from the base of the bill. Found in small parties in the canopy of hill forests and adjacent woods and gardens.

name: Hunter's Cisticola
rangeDescription: High mountains of western kenya, uganda, and northern tanzania
description: A large, plain cisticola with a reddish cap and two bands across the tail tip, one pale and one dark. Found in open montane habitats with thick herbaceous undergrowth, including forest edge, grassland, and heath, almost always in pairs or small groups.

name: Bristle-crowned Starling
rangeDescription: Central ethiopia, northwestern and southern somalia, and northern kenya
description: A large blue-black starling with a fuzzy bump on the forehead. The very long and pointed tail and large red wing panels are conspicuous in flight.

name: Long-billed Plover
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern asia; winters to india and indochina
description: Medium-sized plover. Breeds in flowing rivers with shingle islands and banks; outside of breeding season, can be found in slower rocky rivers, as well as flooded fields and lakeshores.

name: Dunn's Lark
rangeDescription: Southern edge of sahara (mauritania to mali, chad, and central sudan)
description: A chunky, large-billed lark of desolate sandy deserts and open arid plains in northern Africa. Plain sandy-brown above and paler below, with faint and indistinct white markings on the face.

name: Black-eared Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Australia
description: Small plain cuckoo with a dark eye and black
